extracted.intended_audience: marketing, communications, and public relations professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting press releases that get noticed by journalists, stakeholders, and search engines, focusing on headline, length/lead, and timing. Intended to help communications pros make releases concise, searchable, and more likely to be read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline relevance and concision (character limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: As the first thing the reader looks at (and one of the major elements search engines scan), your headline should be relevant and concise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the character length to 88 characters or less, and include the most important keywords in the first 55 to 70 characters. The headline should clearly convey the topic and prioritize the strongest keywords early so both readers and search engines see them immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with why and keep the release concise (~600 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with why: lead with 'why' — as in, why should your audience care?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The longer the press release, the less likely the reader is to read it in its entirety. Try to keep your press releases around 600 words and front-load the most important messages so you get your key points across quickly and concisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: send at off times to stand out
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing is everything: 52% of news is sent on the hour and half hour, with the highest volume of copy sent Tuesdays at 8:00 AM ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break the mold by sending your press releases at off times (for example, 8:47 AM ET) to stand out from the crowd. Avoid peak distribution times (hour/half-hour and major morning spikes) when possible to increase the chance your release will be noticed.
